admin.title: Administration
admin.overview.emptyText: Your role lets you make changes in the administration but not open any of its sections. Ask an owner for read access.
admin.forbidden.title: No access
admin.forbidden.text: Only server admins and organization admins can open the administration.
admin.forbidden.section: You do not have the permission this section needs. Ask an admin of your organization if you need it.
admin.members.title: Members
admin.members.lead: People in this organization and their roles.
admin.members.emailHint: The person needs an account on this server. A server admin creates accounts under Users.
admin.members.removeText: Remove {name} from this organization? They lose access to its dashboards and data sources at once. Their account stays.
admin.members.lastOwner: This is the last owner of the organization. Make another member an owner first; an organization always needs one.
admin.members.cannotGrant: You cannot give a role with permissions you do not have yourself.
admin.members.noAccount: No account uses this email address. A server admin can create one under Users.
admin.members.alreadyMember: This person is already a member.
admin.teams.title: Teams
admin.teams.lead: Groups of members that receive roles and access together.
admin.teams.name: Team name
admin.teams.nameTaken: A team with this name already exists. Choose another name.
admin.teams.empty: No teams yet. Teams let you give several members the same roles and access at once.
admin.teams.deleteText: Delete the team “{name}”? Its members lose the roles and access they had through it. Their accounts and memberships stay.
admin.teams.noMembers: This team has no members yet.
admin.teams.everyoneIn: Every member of the organization is already in this team.
admin.teams.removeMemberText: Remove {name} from “{team}”? They keep their own role in the organization.
admin.teams.teamRoleHint: Maintainers can add and remove members of this team.
admin.teams.rolesLead: Every member of the team gets the permissions of these roles, on top of their own role. At most {count} roles; the owner role cannot be given to a team.
admin.teams.rolesChanged: The roles of the team were changed.
admin.roles.title: Roles
admin.roles.lead: Sets of permissions. The built-in roles are fixed; your own roles combine permissions as you need them.
admin.roles.builtinReadOnly: Built-in roles cannot be changed. Create your own role to combine permissions differently.
admin.roles.name: Name
admin.roles.nameTaken: A role with this name already exists. Choose another name.
admin.roles.nameBuiltin: The names owner, admin, editor and viewer are reserved for the built-in roles Owner, Admin, Editor and Viewer. Choose another name.
admin.roles.nameNotAllowed: This name belongs to a built-in role or is not allowed. Choose another name.
admin.roles.notHeld: You can only give permissions you have yourself.
admin.roles.cannotGrant: You cannot give permissions you do not have yourself.
admin.roles.unknownPermission: A permission this version of the interface does not know yet.
admin.roles.notFound: This role does not exist. It may have been deleted.
admin.roles.deleteText: Delete the role “{name}”? Members and teams that have it lose its permissions.
admin.roles.inUse: This role is still given to members. Give them another role first.
admin.permission.dashboards.read: Open dashboards and see their panels.
admin.permission.dashboards.share: Give users and teams of this organization access to dashboards.
admin.permission.folders.read: See folders and what is in them.
admin.permission.folders.permissions: Decide who may access a folder, including restricted folders.
admin.permission.datasources.query: Run own queries on data sources, for example in Explore.
admin.permission.datasources.read: See data sources and their settings, without secrets.
admin.permission.datasources.write: Add data sources and change their connection settings.
admin.permission.datasources.permissions: Decide who may query or change a data source.
admin.permission.annotations.write: Add notes to points in time on dashboards.
admin.permission.teams.read: See teams and who is in them.
admin.permission.teams.write: Create, rename and delete teams and give them roles.
admin.permission.teams.members: Add members to teams and remove them.
admin.permission.users.read: See the members of the organization, for example to share a dashboard.
admin.permission.users.write: Change the role of members and remove them.
admin.permission.roles.write: Create, change and delete own roles.
admin.permission.serviceaccounts.write: Manage service accounts and their tokens.
admin.permission.audit.read: Read the audit log of the organization.
admin.permission.plugins.configure: Configure the plugins a server admin installed.
admin.permission.settings.read: See the settings of the organization.
admin.permission.settings.write: Change the settings of the organization.
admin.permission.org.delete: Delete the organization with everything in it.
admin.access.title: Access to “{name}”
admin.access.lead.folder: Who may use this folder beyond their role. Access to a folder also applies to its subfolders and dashboards.
admin.access.lead.dashboard: Who may use this dashboard beyond their role.
admin.access.lead.datasource: Who may query or change this data source beyond their role.
admin.access.none: Nobody has extra access. Everyone uses the permissions of their role.
admin.access.cannotPick: You may not see users, teams or roles, so you cannot pick whom to give access.
admin.why.buttonLabel: Why do I have this permission? {permission}
admin.why.title: Where this permission comes from
admin.why.none: You do not have this permission.
admin.settings.empty: There are no settings here yet.
admin.settings.notEditable: This setting cannot be changed here.
admin.settings.noWritePermission: You can see this setting, but not change it.
admin.conflict.title: Changed in the meantime
admin.conflict.text: Someone else saved “{name}” while you were editing the setting. Keep their value, or overwrite it with yours.
admin.orgSettings.title: Organization settings
admin.orgSettings.lead: Settings for everyone in this organization. Changes apply at once.
admin.audit.title: Audit log
admin.audit.lead: Who changed what and when in this organization.
admin.users.title: Users
admin.users.lead: Every account on this server, across organizations.
admin.users.name: Name
admin.users.emailTaken: An account with this email address already exists.
admin.users.locked: {name} is locked and can no longer sign in.
admin.users.removedAdmin: {name} is no longer a server admin.
admin.users.lastServerAdmin: This is the last server admin. Make another user a server admin first; the server always needs one.
admin.orgs.title: Organizations
admin.orgs.name: Organization name
admin.orgs.ownerHint: The first owner manages the new organization. Server admins are not members of every organization.
admin.serverSettings.title: Server settings
admin.serverSettings.lead: Settings for the whole server. Values from the environment or the configuration file take precedence and are shown read-only.
admin.serverSettings.fromEnv: Set by an environment variable on the server. Change it there and restart Kalzit.
admin.serverSettings.fromFile: Set in the configuration file kalzit.toml. Change it there and restart Kalzit.
admin.serverSettings.fileOnly: Only the configuration file or the environment can change this, so a wrong value here cannot lock everyone out.
admin.serverAudit.title: Server audit log
admin.serverAudit.lead: Who changed what and when on this server, across organizations.
admin.account.title: Your account
admin.account.lead: Your name, password, sessions and permissions.
admin.account.name: Name
admin.account.emailHint: A server admin can change it.
admin.account.passwordLead: Changing the password signs you out everywhere else; this browser stays signed in.
admin.account.currentWrong: The current password is not correct.
admin.account.sessionsLead: Browsers where you are signed in.
admin.account.revokeOthersText: End all other sessions? Those browsers have to sign in again.
admin.account.permissionsLead: In {org} you are {role}. What you may do there:
admin.account.noPermissions: You have no permissions in this organization.
admin.common.changedMeanwhile: Not undone: someone else changed this in the meantime. The page now shows the current state.
admin.members.exceedsYou: You can only change or remove members, and give roles, whose permissions you hold yourself.
admin.members.aboveYou: This member's role has permissions you do not have, so you cannot change or remove them.
admin.members.unknownRole: This role does not exist anymore. Reload the page and choose another.
admin.teams.rolesInvalid: The server did not accept these roles. A team can have at most 20 roles, and never the owner role.
admin.teams.rolesExceedYou: This team's roles have permissions you do not have, so you cannot change the team or its members.
admin.teams.rolesAboveYou: The team's roles have permissions you do not have, so you cannot add or remove its members.
admin.teams.rolesRestored: The roles of the team were restored.
admin.roles.limit: This organization already has the most custom roles it can have. Delete one before creating another.
admin.roles.limitReached: This organization has {count} custom roles, the most it can have.
admin.roles.aboveYou: This role has permissions you do not have, so you cannot change or delete it.
admin.roles.ownerOnly: Only the built-in owner role has this.
admin.access.cannotGrant: You can only give access up to what you may do on this yourself.
admin.access.cannotSee: You cannot see who has access to this. Ask someone who manages its access.
admin.settings.rejected: The server did not accept this value. Check it and try again.
admin.audit.toBeforeFrom: Choose an end date on or after the start date.
admin.why.grantAbove: Access “{level}” on a folder above, given to {subject}
admin.users.lockText: Lock {name}? They are signed out everywhere at once and cannot sign in until you unlock them.
admin.users.demoteSelfText: You lose access to the server administration at once and cannot undo this yourself. Another server admin has to give the role back.
admin.users.setPasswordText: The user is signed out everywhere and signs in with the new password.
admin.orgs.ownerGone: This account does not exist anymore. Choose another owner.
admin.orgs.noOwner: There is no account that can sign in to own the organization. Create or unlock a user first.
admin.users.cannotLock: This account cannot be locked: it is the last server admin, or the last owner of an organization who can sign in. Give that role to someone else first.
admin.settings.datasources.sqlite_dirs.d: Folders on the server from which SQLite data sources may open database files. The data folder is always refused. If the list is empty, no SQLite files are allowed.
admin.settings.datasources.allowed_targe: If this list is not empty, data sources may only connect to these hosts and networks.
admin.settings.datasources.query_timeout: How long a single query may run before it is stopped.
admin.settings.datasources.max_rows.desc: The most rows, points, documents or nodes a single query returns.
admin.settings.datasources.max_response_: The largest result one request may produce, with all its queries together.
admin.settings.datasources.max_parallel_: How many queries run at once on the whole server. Further ones wait for a free slot, at most until their time limit runs out.
admin.settings.datasources.max_inflight_: How much memory the results of all running queries may take together.
admin.settings.audit.retention_days.desc: Audit events are deleted after this many days, since they can hold client addresses.
admin.settings.appearance.default_langua: Language of the UI for users who have not chosen one.
Theme of the UI for users who have not chosen one.
admin.settings.sessions.lifetime_hours.d: A session ends this many hours after sign-in.
admin.settings.sessions.idle_timeout_hou: A session ends after this many hours without a request. 0 means never.
admin.settings.dashboards.version_retent: Versions kept per dashboard; older ones are deleted on save. 0 keeps all.
admin.settings.dashboards.default_time_r: Time range of new dashboards in this organization.
